summary: Twelve comment-endorsed tools, services, books, films, and devices from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: FluidVoice
items.source_story_title: Desert Ant Labs: local, fast models that run on device
items.summary: An offline macOS dictation app built around local speech-to-text models.
items.why_included: A commenter testing offline dictation apps directly called FluidVoice great.
items.evidence: The commenter singled out FluidVoice as a great app for local dictation.

evidence_sources.author: shelled
evidence_sources.excerpt: If any of you are interested there are apps like https://github.com/altic-dev/FluidVoice (this one's a great app)

items.name: Print for Visual Studio Code
items.summary: A VS Code extension for printing source code and Markdown documents.
items.why_included: A commenter searching for code-printing support reported that this extension worked well.
items.evidence: The commenter identified pdconsec.vscode-print as an option that worked well.

evidence_sources.author: rrr_oh_man
evidence_sources.excerpt: This one seems to work well: pdconsec.vscode-print

items.name: GNU Radio World
items.summary: A browser-based GNU Radio flowgraph editor and WebAssembly runtime.
items.why_included: A commenter praised the interface and planned to keep experimenting with it.
items.evidence: The commenter found the GUI pleasant and called the project awesome.

evidence_sources.author: baileynoack
evidence_sources.excerpt: The GUI is pretty nice to interact with. I'll definitely be playing around with this some more, awesome project!

items.name: Read the Docs
items.source_story_title: Understanding the recent DDoS attack against Read the Docs
items.summary: A platform for building, versioning, searching, and hosting software documentation.
items.why_included: A frequent user called the service fantastic after years of practical use.
items.evidence: The commenter said they use Read the Docs often and praised it as fantastic.

evidence_sources.author: tescreal
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use your site (with a manual transmission user-agent) often, and it's fantastic.

items.name: Crowd Supply
items.summary: A crowdfunding and fulfillment platform focused on original hardware projects.
items.why_included: A repeat buyer reported consistently good outcomes and unusually high trust.
items.evidence: The commenter had bought several projects through Crowd Supply and had never been disappointed.

evidence_sources.author: utopiah
evidence_sources.excerpt: I bought quite a few projects via CS and never been disappointed.

items.name: Zinwa Q25
items.summary: A BlackBerry Classic-style Android phone rebuilt with modern internal hardware.
items.why_included: An owner explicitly said they loved theirs after installing a newer Android build.
items.evidence: The commenter praised their modernized BlackBerry Classic and said they loved it.

evidence_sources.author: xethos
evidence_sources.excerpt: there are currently BlackBerry Classic shipping with modern internals. I love mine

items.name: Incorruptible
items.summary: Eric Ries's book on keeping successful companies aligned with their missions.
items.why_included: A commenter highly recommended its account of shareholder primacy and corporate corruption.
items.evidence: The commenter highly recommended the book for its explanation of how markets can corrupt companies.

evidence_sources.author: sethherr
evidence_sources.excerpt: I highly recommend Incorruptible by Eric Reis - it makes it clear that shareholder primacy is a relatively recent phenomena

items.name: The Elephant in the Brain
items.source_story_title: Claude, change the “Add to Cart” button to blue
items.summary: A book about hidden motives behind everyday behavior and social institutions.
items.why_included: A commenter gave the book a direct and emphatic recommendation.
items.evidence: The commenter said the lesson came from the book and strongly recommended it.

evidence_sources.author: BurningFrog
evidence_sources.excerpt: I learned this from "The Elephant in the Brain", which I strongly recommend

items.name: The Devastating Decline of a Brilliant Young Coder
items.source_story_title: A Biography of Lee Holloway, the Architect of Cloudflare's Technology (Part 1)
items.summary: A Wired profile of Cloudflare cofounder Lee Holloway's life and illness.
items.why_included: A commenter highly recommended the long, heartbreaking profile.
items.evidence: The commenter directly recommended Wired's profile and described it as heartbreaking.

evidence_sources.author: zachthewf
evidence_sources.excerpt: Highly recommend the Wired story about Lee

items.name: Coyote vs. Acme
items.summary: A live-action and animated comedy built around Wile E. Coyote's lawsuit.
items.why_included: A viewer enthusiastically recommended the film after seeing it in theaters.
items.evidence: The commenter called the film very funny and entertaining and strongly recommended it.

evidence_sources.author: hurtbaseball
evidence_sources.excerpt: I can't recommend the movie enough. Saw it over the weekend and it's very funny and entertaining.

items.name: Who Framed Roger Rabbit
items.summary: A live-action and animated film-noir comedy set in 1947 Hollywood.
items.why_included: A viewer recommended it over the newly released Coyote vs. Acme film.
items.evidence: The commenter explicitly preferred and recommended Who Framed Roger Rabbit in comparison.

evidence_sources.author: EGreg
evidence_sources.excerpt: I would recommend “who framed Roger Rabbit” over this.

items.name: Dr. Strangelove
items.summary: Stanley Kubrick's dark comedy about nuclear brinkmanship and institutional absurdity.
items.why_included: A commenter described the film as always worth watching again.
items.evidence: The commenter directly endorsed Dr. Strangelove as worthy of repeat viewing.

evidence_sources.author: sdl
evidence_sources.excerpt: Always worth watching again: "Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb"
